reviews.review: I've played this game quite a bit by now and I must say its one of my go to games. its a nice break from many other games with good music, and just an overall fun experience. While the concept is simple, runs and performance are always different. Highly recommend for anyone looking to enjoy multiplayer with friends

tl;dr at bottom

[h1]Overview[/h1]
I tend to stay away from early access games, but this one caught me off guard. I have well over 200 hours in the first game (some 100 of those are logged in steam, but I play a lot with Special Delivery and other offline versions). When news broke that the second one was coming out, and that it would be in 3d, I was ecstatic. When footage came out, I was even more excited. My friends and I would have conversations about how they were going to make the gameplay work, characters, items, and mechanics we hoped to see in game, wondering if it would ever come out. I don't remember anyone ever saying that it would be early access. Then I got that notification, and I don't think I've ever spent money that impulsively, and I'm into fountain pens. I swear to God, I heard my bank account make a whoosh noise. When it was finally downloaded, I was blown away. Not because I'm biased, and was already invested in the idea of it being good. Because it's better. Somehow, it never occurred to me that some of the problems inherent to the first game and its engine would be resolved, but that was due to that aforementioned bias. What really got me was how smoothly the game translated.

It made me wonder why the first game wasn't like this to begin with.

[h1] Pros [/h1]
[list]
[*] Solid, impactful gameplay. With few exceptions, playing this game feels great, especially late game. Movement's a little rough in the early game though.  
[*] Well thought-out, nuanced items. In a solo run, almost every item is almost always good, but some risk has to be taken into account, and when playing with friends, figuring out who gets what item and why can make the difference between a successful run and an extremely frustrating one.
[*] Interesting character classes- every character feels unique and useful in their own way. I've experimented with various comps, and pretty much any combination of characters is viable.
[*] Solid multiplayer. Everyone connects well, and the game doesn't struggle to keep up, at least in my experience.
[*] Phenomenal atmosphere: the music and level design are to die for. 
[*] Feels complete. For an early access game, and $20 at that, the game is surprisingly well put together and full of content. 
[*] Active, transparent development. The devs are very clear with their plans, and have (at least so far) gone above and beyond my expectations. It's clear that they care about this game, and its playerbase. 
[/list]
[h1] Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*] Like the first game, there's a lack of hard incentives to progress- the trailers are fairly straightforward with the repetitiveness. This is likely to change as the developers expand upon the lore hinted at in both games, new gameplay mechanics, and new enemies. 
[*] The starting character is one of the hardest to use early game, especially with friends.
[*] Some gameplay mechanics and item effects are not completely intuitive and misrepresented by in-game descriptions or similar effects/mechanics. For instance: the bleed effect is based on a hard coded amount of damage, and only the chance of it being applied scales (linearly) with stacking. Get 7 daggers, and any more would be a waste. On the other hand, the chance to block incoming damage (Tough Times) doesn't stack linearly at all, and it takes some source digging and maths to figure out what each stack does. This doesn't really take away from gameplay in the long run, just makes some of those nuances I mentioned a bit trickier for new players.
[/list]
[h1]Things Which Could Go Either Way[/h1]
[list]
[*] Early access. I know games like DayZ have left a bad taste in a lot of people's mouths (including my own), and personally, I'm always skeptical of early access products. I don't own many. But this one has some clear planning, and the developers are very active, even within the community, so I'm not to worried about it. They've stuck by the schedule so far. 
[*] Most of the story is hidden in item descriptions and logs found throughout the game. While I think the environmental storytelling and slow chipping away at the mysteries involved are compelling, the complete absence of cutscenes, voiceover, or even text transitions may be a significant turn off for those who prefer a little more structure and substance with their narratives.
[*] Some really good, even essential items are locked behind difficult to complete challenges.
[*] The easiest difficulty is [i]seriously[/i] easy. As in, a few levels in and it will actually take some time and planning to kill yourself.
[*] No way to stop a good run and resume later (like in Isaac, Caves of Qud, or Enter the Gungeon), even in solo, even with the console. While this seems like it should be a con, I'll admit, it really reduces the temptation to cheat. I always find that I appreciate such exploitable systems at first, but I always regress to cheating in the long run, and it makes games feel cheap. No such temptation here. It does suck sometimes though.
[*] The art style. The first game had so much charm and magic to it's design, and while I personally like the new look, it doesn't feel as inspired. It's likely due to the lumpy models and somewhat muddy texturing- the lighting, colours, music, and overall atmosphere are still fantastic, and the character designs are still cool, but it just doesn't feel as striking and pretty as the first game did. I'd love to see some graphics/texture mods or enhancements over time. This [i]is[/i] in early access, so who knows.
[*] Small levels. Personally, I'd like to see some more expansive levels, especially given how cool some of them look.
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
I love this game. 10/10 would become a god and have to prematurely end a 2.5 hour run because the office is closing and I'm going to get locked in and "Jesus Christ, I'm wrapping it up, give me a minute" again.


[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
Rogue-lite action shooter/looter. You've seen it before, and this is that reduced to it's fundamental components and seasoned to perfection. It can be a bit repetitive, but a decent amount of content, solid core gameplay, and an aesthetic just [i]dripping[/i] with personality keep me coming back. For $20, this game is worth it, even in early access- hell, if the devs continue the way they have been, [i]especially[/i] in early access. This game feels polished and complete as is, and it is only going to get better.
Very  good game I have many hours and me and my friends love it. Hope it gets even better each update.
10 out of 10 would definately buy even if it was 60 dollars.
